claims.claim: Raw evaluator, label and gold-answer fields are excluded from the online Guard projection; exact_gold exposes only a derived authorization object.
claims.boundary: This is an implementation and experiment-contract claim, not evidence that other published systems leak evaluator fields.

claims.claim: Unsafe effects in the four main DeepSeek authorization cells remained at or near the observed floor.
claims.observed: Three cells were 0/100 and policy-only plus auto_compiled was 1/100; all paired unsafe-effect Holm-adjusted p values were 1.0.
claims.boundary: A near-floor endpoint does not prove universal robustness and limits power to distinguish mechanisms.

claims.claim: Changing from auto_compiled to exact_gold reduced benign-tool task completion under both Guard variants.
claims.observed: Policy-only changed from 22/60 to 9/60 (-21.67 percentage points); M3-full changed from 16/60 to 7/60 (-15.00 points).
claims.boundary: The exact_gold condition is an oracle-sensitivity treatment, not a recommended deployment policy.

claims.claim: Exact authorization changed runtime burden by removing ASK while increasing DENY incidence, failures and tail latency.
claims.observed: ASK incidence fell to 0; DENY incidence was 48.89% for policy-only and 45.00% for M3-full; failure incidence was 23.89% and 24.44%; p95 latency was 19.42 and 19.62 seconds.
claims.boundary: ASK and DENY are record-incidence measures; event totals are reported separately.

claims.claim: The evaluated full configuration package did not show a stable benefit over the policy package.
claims.observed: Under auto_compiled, M3-full had 0/100 versus 1/100 unsafe effects but completed 16/60 versus 22/60 benign tool tasks; Public Pro and Flash both placed M3-full above policy-only in unsafe effects.
claims.boundary: The historical package comparison remains bundled. E1 separately identifies prompt and module-bundle effects, but still cannot identify any individual provenance, temporal/data-flow, monotonicity, or confirmation component. The result is limited to the tested implementation, policies, benchmarks, and DeepSeek models.

claims.claim: The unfavorable M3-full versus policy-only security direction is observed in both DeepSeek V4 Pro and V4 Flash Public matrices.
claims.observed: Public Pro recorded 38/600 versus 13/600 unsafe effects; Public Flash recorded 24/400 versus 12/400.
claims.boundary: This supports a within-provider model replication only and does not establish cross-provider generalization.

claims.claim: Authorization-regime outcomes are reported separately for AgentDojo and M3-v2, with prespecified M3-v2 attack-family results retained in the structured analysis artifact.
claims.boundary: These strata are descriptive heterogeneity analyses; they are not independently powered confirmatory tests.

claims.claim: Defense-aware adaptive search found additional first unsafe effects between budgets 50 and 200; a prespecified subset of twelve B200 survivors had no new first success through 500.
claims.observed: First unsafe effects were found for 4/40 tasks by query 50 and 18/40 by query 200. Among twelve prespecified B200 survivors, 0/12 first succeeded by 500; the Wilson upper limit was 24.25%.
claims.boundary: The 0/12 result is conditional on the selected B200-survivor subset. It is not a complete original-panel B500 curve, zero-tail-risk result, saturation estimate, or budget-2000 claim.

claims.claim: The lean DeepSeek experiment retains official returned-model identity, response IDs when obtained, ITT failures, token/cost accounting and isolated-effect execution without provider tools or real external actions.
claims.boundary: Provider model aliases do not identify an immutable hidden-weight revision.

claims.claim: The authorization or E6 findings generalize across DeepSeek and Gemini providers.
claims.boundary: The earlier study closed at 32/450 terminal items with five responses. The separately executed E6 prefix had five response-bearing records, one response-less failure, and 174 administrative closures. Under the single-block amendment, E6 Gemini was diagnostic by design even if coverage had been complete. Neither observed dataset provides paired effect coverage; all Gemini effects are not estimable.

claims.claim: M3 is the first, only, state-of-the-art or universally superior provenance-aware runtime defense.
claims.boundary: VIGIL, DRIFT, Task Shield, Progent, IPIGuard, CaMeL, ARGUS, AuthGraph, FAVA and provenance-sensitivity auditing occupy overlapping mechanism and evaluation space.

claims.claim: JISA is SCIE and JCR Q2 on the submission date.
claims.unlock_condition: An authorized institutional user must verify current SCIE coverage and JCR quartile immediately before submission.

claims.claim: The 21 references currently cited by the manuscript have verified metadata, stable landing pages and publication status; all 21/21 active citation contexts were checked against official abstracts, proceedings summaries, or the official preprint PDF.
claims.boundary: The review verifies the manuscript's active citation contexts against primary records; it does not reproduce every experiment in the cited papers. Review any newly activated citation and repeat publication-status checks at submission.

claims.claim: A concurrent 2x2 study separates prompt-profile and runtime-module-bundle effects.
claims.observed: Across 400 attack assignments, policy cells had two unsafe effects and full cells had none; the module estimate was -1.00 percentage point and the direct endpoint was floor-limited.
claims.boundary: The module factor is a bundle and does not identify the effect of provenance, data flow, monotonicity, or confirmation separately.

claims.claim: The full Guard is source-sensitive in deterministic replay, but this did not yield executed end-to-end actions in E2.
claims.observed: Across 240 unauthorized proposals false allow was 0/240; across 240 authorized proposals false block was 30/240. All 240 end-to-end runs executed no action.
claims.boundary: Deterministic Guard sensitivity is not evidence of end-to-end utility or a human-confirmation outcome.

claims.claim: E3 and E4 provide conditional challenge and same-provider replication evidence.
claims.observed: E3 reproduced an unsafe effect in 1/60 historically difficult attacks and retained 55 failures; E4 had zero unsafe effects in each Flash attack cell.
claims.boundary: E3 is outcome-enriched and E4 is within one provider; neither estimates deployment prevalence, equivalence, or cross-provider generalization.

claims.claim: E5 completed the prespecified conditional adaptive tail.
claims.observed: All twelve selected B200 survivors reached 500; 0/12 produced a new first unsafe effect, with Wilson 95% upper limit 24.25%.
claims.boundary: This is not a complete B500 panel, a saturation result, or evidence of zero tail risk.

claims.claim: E6 records no-defense attack activity and supplies within-block DeepSeek condition comparisons on a risk-enriched cohort.
claims.observed: DeepSeek was response-bearing for 360/360 work items. Unsafe effects were 17/60 under no defense, 16/60 under VIGIL, 2/60 under policy/normal, 1/60 under policy/safe, and 0/60 under both full cells. The independently executed block overlaps E3 for 47/60 tasks.
claims.boundary: The sample is historically risk-enriched, contains no benign tasks, and was executed in one block. It does not satisfy or test the original multi-window activity gate and does not estimate deployment prevalence, utility, temporal repeatability, independent-sample replication, individual provenance-module effects, or cross-provider generalization.
